ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14; Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14; Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 02/2022/QH15 (effective 1 March 2023); Decree No. 19/2023/ND-CP on AML/CFT implementation; Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN of the State Bank of Viet Nam; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration; Civil Code No. 91/2015/QH14; Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (private LLC member register maintained at the company and filed as part of charter data with the National Business Registration Database; not publicly searchable. Nominee shareholding is not recognized under Vietnamese law - the registered and beneficial owner must be identical for foreign-invested LLCs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Business Registration Certificate of the corporate foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the foreign investor's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Viet Nam has been a party to the Hague Apostille Convention since 1 February 2010) or consular legalization through the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and statutory declaration of beneficial ownership for each individual UBO holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary public / competent authority of the investor's jurisdiction of origin, followed by Vietnamese-language certified translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; Vietnamese notarization of the translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign bank reference letter evidencing financial capacity of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified Vietnamese translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the pre-incorporation filing agent in Viet Nam
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor (corporate signatories or individual UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization abroad plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization; Vietnamese notarization of the translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence under Law on AML 2022, Decree 19/2023/ND-CP and Circular 09/2023/TT-NHNN; obligatory screening of all UBOs, legal representatives and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the Vietnamese counter-terrorism and financial sanctions list, and PEP databases including family members and close associates; standard-risk tier for ISIC 7490 localization agency but foreign-investor shareholder profile triggers level-two CDD on origination of funds and payment rails (Wise B2B and Payoneer are treated as non-bank PSP channels requiring enhanced transaction monitoring and documentary support).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (NBRS) of the Ministry of Planning and Investment - https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn, with integrated submission via the National Public Service Portal https://dichvucong.gov.vn and the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) one-stop registration system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The enterprise name must be expressed in the Vietnamese alphabet (quoc ngu script), be pronounceable in Vietnamese, and may contain Arabic numerals and symbols; a foreign-language name is permitted only as a transliteration or functional equivalent of the Vietnamese name and must be consistent across the charter, seal and invoices. For the localization agency (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541930), the business lines may be described in English in the enterprise registration dossier, but all statutory charter documents, the Enterprise Registration Certificate and the seal inscription are issued in Vietnamese; non-Vietnamese text must be accompanied by a certified translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise; the name must contain 'Công ty TNHH' / 'Cong ty TNHH' (Limited Liability Company identifier)

Names of state agencies, people's armed forces, political organizations, socio-political organizations, or units of the public administration without the prior written consent of the competent authority
Terms contrary to national historical traditions, culture, ethics or fine customs, or that carry national-security-sensitive connotations

Sectoral sensitive tokens requiring prior conditional license or ministerial confirmation: 'Bank/Ngan hang', 'Insurance/Bao hiem', 'Securities/Chung khoan', 'Finance/Tai chinh', 'Audit/Kiem toan', 'Legal consultancy/Tu van phap luat', 'Pharmaceuticals/Duoc pham', 'Education/Giao duc', 'Telecommunications/Vien thong'

The term 'Viet Nam' as a leading trade-name element requires the enterprise to be directly engaged in a nationally significant industry and the written consent of the Ministry of Planning and Investment
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Viet Nam operates no standalone name-reservation instrument; name clearance is decided within 3 working days of submission of the ERO dossier, and an informal name-availability printout from the NBRS portal is treated as a 30-day pre-clearance. Upon rejection, the DPI issues a notice stating the confusing similarity or prohibited token; the applicant must amend the draft charter and re-submit online. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may file a first-instance administrative complaint to the Director of the provincial DPI within 90 days of receiving the refusal (Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13); a second-instance complaint may be lodged with the Business Registration Agency of the Ministry of Planning and Investment; judicial review may thereafter be sought under the Law on Administrative Procedure No. 24/2015/QH14 before the provincial People's Court, subject to exhaustion of all administrative remedies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally restricted for foreign-invested LLCs. The registered head office must be a real, tangible address in the province of registration and must be lawfully possessed by the enterprise under a lease or ownership instrument. Pure mailbox addresses are rejected by the DPI. Serviced-office and co-working leases are accepted only where the premises physically exist, are staffed during business hours, and a full circle lease agreement and landlord consent for enterprise registration are submitted. A home-office address is not acceptable for a foreign-invested localization agency; a commercial office lease is recommended to satisfy the DPI's physical-presence expectations and to support e-invoicing registration and the tax authority's commercial-substance review, given the target payment rails (Wise B2B and Payoneer) are classified as non-bank PSP channels that may trigger additional document requests.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% - Low-to-moderate risk of an unannounced on-site verification within the first 24 months. The DPI rarely inspects translation/dubbing LLCs at registration; however, the General Department of Taxation, market management authorities and payment-supervision bodies may conduct head-office verification visits, particularly where the enterprise claims zero-rated cross-border service exports, applies for e-invoice release, or where the registered address is shared by multiple unrelated enterprises.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Circular 130/2016/TT-BTC (VND 100,000 equivalent); many provinces waive the fee for initial registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial DPI or Management Board of Industrial/Economic Zones

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the investor's country of origin and/or Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille/legalization tariff of the issuing state plus courier and handling charges; market benchmark of US$ 50-60 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation into Vietnamese and notarization of corporate documents, passport and bank reference letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Vietnamese translation company and public notary office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of VND 50,000-200,000 per translated/notarized page plus VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel retainers for incorporation dossier drafting, UBO piercing and AML/CFT compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent foreign-investment law firm (prevailing market rate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for full-service foreign-invested LLC incorporation in Ha Noi or Ho Chi Minh City, including charter drafting, member register preparation and name-clearance support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Business Registration Portal (Business Registration Agency, MPI)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (Enterprise Law 2020), effective 1 January 2021, in particular Articles 22 (conditions for enterprise registration), 25 (application documentation), 44 (mandatory charter contents), 45 (charter content requirements for LLCs), 47 (three-working-day issuance deadline for Enterprise Registration Certificate), 50 (right to reject and procedural recourse), 72-89 (limited liability company formation, members, charter capital), 75 (obligation to contribute charter capital within 90 days), and 196 (registered office and corporate seal). Elaborated by Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration; for foreign investors, Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 36-37 and Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP on market access conditions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Agency of the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI) as the overarching body; operational authority exercised through the Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) where the Company's registered office is located; online filings are accepted via the National Enterprise Registration Portal (thongtindoanhnghiep.gov.vn).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giay de nghi dang ky doanh nghiep) under Form I-1 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, submitted together with Form I-2 (Company Charter) and member identity instruments; the DPI issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate (Giay chung nhan dang ky doanh nghiep) as the conclusive incorporation title.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum charter capital is fixed for multilingual localization activities under ISIC 7490, which constitute a non-conditional business line; accordingly, members may declare a charter capital appropriate to the venture. The declared charter capital must, however, be paid in full within ninety (90) days from the date of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate (Article 75, Law No. 59/2020/QH14); no escrow account or bank-locked deposit is independently required. Foreign investors are permitted 100% ownership and are not subject to a capital floor under Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP for this scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1/2025 OF THE FIRST MEMBERS' MEETING OF [FULL LEGAL NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY

ADOPTED ON [date] AT [registered office address, Viet Nam]

WHEREAS: (i) the Company is a multi-member limited liability company to be formed under Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14; (ii) the Company's permissible scope includes multilingual translation, localization, and media dubbing (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541930); and (iii) the members have resolved to complete the statutory incorporation and to constitute the first governing organs.

NOW, THEREFORE, THE MEMBERS UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

1. Charter Capital and Subscription. The initial charter capital is fixed at VND [amount] (USD [amount]) and is apportioned among the member(s) as set out in Schedule A. Each member irrevocably subscribes to the allocated parts and covenants to contribute them in full, in cash or contributed assets, no later than ninety (90) days from issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.

2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is established at [full address, ward, district, province, Viet Nam], and the Members' Meeting approves the verified lease and confirms the premises as lawful for the purposes of Article 196 of Law No. 59/2020/QH14.

3. Appointment of Officers. The Members' Meeting appoints (a) [Full Name, Passport No.] as the first legal representative (Director/General Director) with independent representation authority and sign-off powers under the Enterprise Law; and (b) [Full Name, Passport No.] as the Chief Accountant/Controller. All officers are granted authority to execute incorporation filings, open bank accounts, procure seals, register taxes, and engage the certified intermediary service providers.

4. Filing Authorizations. The legal representative is expressly authorized to prepare, sign, notarize, lodge and pursue the Application for Enterprise Registration, the Investment Registration Certificate application, tax registration, seal notification, and all ancillary registrations with the Department of Planning and Investment, National Enterprise Registration Portal and tax authorities.

5. Governance Pending Further Meetings. The Company shall operate under the annexed interim by-laws until the next Members' Meeting; pre-incorporation contracts entered into on behalf of the Company within the preceding month are ratified to the fullest extent permitted by law.

6. Effective Date. This Resolution is immediately effective as of the date of signature and remains in force until rescinded or replaced.

Signed by all members and the appointed legal representative on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and verification of the registered office premises and lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Notary Public Office (Pho cong chung) licensed by the Department of Justice; premises title verification supported by the Department of Natural Resources and Environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Identify an office/commercial premises; obtain the landlord's title document (GCN qsd dat/so huu) and construction completion certificate; execute a written office lease in Vietnamese, notarize the lease at a provincial notary office; verify that the address is not used by another enterprise and that the building legally permits office/service activity. The notarized lease and certified copies are core exhibits for both the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate filings.
required_dossiers: Executed office lease agreement (Vietnamese original and English translation)
Landlord's certificate of ownership/use rights (certified copy)
Landlord's corporate registration certificate (if landlord is an entity)
Construction completion or fire-safety certificate of the building (as applicable)
Passport/citizen ID of notarization applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses due to incomplete title documentation, procure a certified extract from the land registrar or substitute a notarized letter of permission from the registered owner; if the address already appears on a conflicting enterprise record, request deregistration of the previous occupant from the DPI or choose an alternative address and re-notarize.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) application for foreign-invested shareholding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Registration Division, Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province/city where the project is located; specially administered by an industrial/EPZ Authority where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where any member is a foreign investor, submit an IRC application under Article 32 of the Investment Law 2020 via the online or physical one-stop shop; the dossier must identify the project (multilingual localization office), capital, location, and market access position; DPI screens against Decree 31/2021/ND-CP, confirms no conditional sectors apply, and issues the IRC within 15 working days; the ERC application may in practice be lodged concurrently with the IRC dossier or immediately after IRC issuance in the same one-stop window.
required_dossiers: Investment registration application form (Form A.I-3/II-3 of Decree 31/2021/ND-CP)
Investment project proposal / business plan
Certificate of legal status of investor (passport or certificate of incorporation of corporate shareholder)
Financial proof of investor capacity (audited financials or bank reference)
Notarized office lease and lawful premises title
Documentation of market access compliance statement for ISIC 7490
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For non-conditional activities, DPI cannot lawfully reject without citing a specific statutory ground; upon a written request for clarification, the applicant corrects and resubmits within the fixed deadline (typically 10 working days); any formal refusal may be appealed to the Director of DPI within 30 days and thereafter to the provincial People's Committee or to an administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, provincial Department of Planning and Investment; online via the National Enterprise Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form I-1 (Application for Enterprise Registration) together with Form I-2 (Charter) and member list; attach certified copies of the IRC, passport/legal certificates of all members, notarized lease, and the first resolution appointing the legal representative; submit online through the National Enterprise Registration Portal or in person at the DPI one-stop counter; upon a complete dossier, the DPI must issue the ERC within 3 working days; upon issuance the Company obtains its legal personality, enterprise tax code, and stable business identification.
required_dossiers: Form I-1 — Application for Enterprise Registration
Form I-2 — Company Charter (approved by the Members' Meeting)
Form I-3 — List of members / list of legal representatives (as applicable)
Valid certified copies of identity instruments of each member
Notarized office lease and title documents
Investment Registration Certificate (for foreign investors)
Member Resolution on officers and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues an amendment requirement under Article 51 of Decree 01/2021/ND-CP, incorporate the correction and resubmit within the notified deadline (usually 10-15 days); if the response is rejected, the applicant may demand written reasons and file a complaint under the Law on Complaints (No. 02/2011/QH13) or bring an administrative action; in case the online portal times out, resort to the physical one-stop submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal, tax registration and legal representative disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed seal-engraving establishment registered with the Ministry of Public Security; General Department of Taxation / provincial Tax Sub-Department; Business Registration Office for seal specimen notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Post-ERC, the Company orders a corporate seal from a government-licensed seal-engraving shop; a preservation and custody policy is adopted; within 3 working days after the ERC, the legal representative must notify the DPI of the seal specimen via the National Enterprise Registration Portal; simultaneously, tax registration is completed automatically with the tax code printed on the ERC, but a value-added tax/payroll information file must be activated with the Tax Sub-Department; if a separate sub-entity or office is established, obtain a dependent tax code.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Company seal specimen notification (Form I-16 of Decree 01/2021/ND-CP)
ID of the legal representative and other officers
Seal engraver's license and invoice
Tax registration activation form (if used) and the company's email/account on the taxation e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal notification is rejected due to illegible specimen, re-notify within the corrected timeframe; if the automatic tax code is not updated, visit the Tax Sub-Department with the ERC and IRC to obtain a written confirmation; any reactivation or issuance of the enterprise TIN can be escalated in writing to the Chief Tax Officer, who must act within the administrative service deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening, charter capital contribution and labour/social insurance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Vietnamese or foreign branch banks (for corporate and Foreign Investment Capital Accounts); Vietnam Social Security (provincial agency) and the DPI for capital contribution confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the project capital/current bank account with the appointed bank in Viet Nam; if the Company is foreign-invested, also open a Foreign Investment Capital Account (FICA), and financial transactions in VND/documents must comply with the State Bank of Vietnam rules; members must contribute all subscribed capital within 90 days from the ERC; after contribution, file an amended contribution status to the DPI; finally, register the employer with Vietnam Social Security, adopt work rules, record labour contracts and arrange occupational safety training in accordance with Law No. 84/2015/QH13.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate and IRC (where applicable)
Members' Resolution on opening bank accounts and capital confirmation
Charter capital contribution schedule and source-of-funds documentation
Passports/identity documents of authorised signatories
Labour contracts, salary scales and social insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening awaiting law-enforcement database confirmation, the Company submits a fresh resolution and an apostilled board authorization to the bank's legal department; if social insurance registration fails on the data-matching system, use the e-Government one-stop portal to synchronise the enterprise code and provide corrected personal identification of employees; incomplete capital contribution within 90 days is cured by filing the updated charter capital status with the DPI and re-documenting the funding plan to avoid deregulation sanctions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is triggered. Multilingual localization (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541930) is a non-conditional service activity. The only relevant formation-level bodies are the Department of Planning and Investment (Business Registration Office and Investment Registration Division), the Ministry of Planning and Investment for market-access interpretation, and the Department of Construction for premises occupation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. The Enterprise Registration Certificate (Giay chung nhan dang ky doanh nghiep) and, where foreign equity exists, the Investment Registration Certificate (Giay chung nhan dang ky dau tu) constitute the complete operating authorization. No separate manufacturing or professional operational license is issued by any industrial board.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) through the delegated provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE); commune-level People's Committee for environmental protection registration of small non-manufacturing projects
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Group IV under Article 28 and Appendix V of Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP — the localization studio is a non-industrial, office-based activity and is therefore exempt from preparing a formal Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report. The project holder need only file a simplified environmental protection registration (Dang ky bao ve moi truong) with the competent authority where wastewater, dust, exhaust or hazardous waste generated at the premises require management; no environmental permit under Articles 40-42 of the Law on Environmental Protection No. 72/2020/QH14 is required below the permit thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater must meet QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT for on-site treatment prior to discharge to municipal sewers; industrial-grade emissions, if any IPCC solvent-based dubbing or printing support activity is introduced, must satisfy QCVN 20:2009/BTNMT (air emissions for industrial processes) and QCVN 19:2009/BTNMT; hazardous waste must be classified, labelled and transferred to licensed treatment contractors in accordance with Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP and Circular No. 02/2022/TT-BTNMT, with written manifests retained for at least 5 years; municipal solid waste must be contracted with the local urban environment company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) of the Ministry of Finance, Socialist Republic of Viet Nam; national e-Tax portal: https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn (legacy portal: thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn); customs export declaration authority: General Department of Vietnam Customs (Tổng cục Hải quan) operating the VNACCS/VCIS national single window and the Vietnam National Single Window (NSW) for trade facilitation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested Limited Liability Company obtains its Tax Identification Number (MST - Mã số thuế) without a standalone tax registration application because Vietnam operates an integrated enterprise-and-tax registration mechanism. Procedure: (1) obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment or the relevant Industrial Zone / Export Processing Zone authority for new foreign-invested projects; (2) file the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) application containing the charter, list of members, legal representative and headquarters address; (3) the General Department of Taxation automatically issues the MST upon ERC issuance, in accordance with Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on business registration and the Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14; (4) activate the e-Tax account on the national e-Tax portal and register for electronic invoice issuing status in the General Department of Taxation's invoice registration system; (5) open a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) and a general current account at a licensed commercial bank; (6) if exporting or importing physical goods or media, register as a customs declarant through the VNACCS/VCIS system and obtain a customs code; the MST is the uniform identifier for all CIT, VAT, PIT withholding, Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT), customs and social insurance filings. For localization activities with no physical import-export, only e-Tax and e-invoice activation are required; a customs registration is not necessary unless media masters or hardware cross borders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam does not operate a check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections: (a) VAT method election: an LLC may elect the credit/deduction method only when its annual revenue exceeds VND 1 billion, but a newly incorporated LLC meeting accounting standards may voluntarily register for the deduction method; firms under the threshold use the direct method on invoiced added value unless they elect the deduction method. (b) Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) election: a foreign service provider with a PE or an enterprise contracting cross-border can elect the 'normal VAT/CIT filing method' or the 'deemed assessment method' for withholding purposes; the deemed method is mandatory unless a valid Vietnamese tax registration and proper books are demonstrated. (c) Foreign Tax Credit election: resident LLCs may elect to credit or deduct qualifying foreign income taxes on worldwide income; no deemed-paid credit is available for dividends from foreign subsidiaries beyond treaty/legislative provisions. (d) CIT incentive election: an eligible EPE/High-Tech/Industrial-Zone project must file a tax registration addendum and apply for a CIT incentive certificate (exemption for up to 4 years, 50% reduction for the next 9 years, standard rates of 10%, 15% or 17% depending on zone and scale); the election is made by indicating the incentive within the self-assessment return. (e) Loss carryforward is mandatory and non-elective: losses offset against income over the next 5 consecutive years, with no carryback. No group consolidation election exists; no hybrid-election mechanism is available because Decree No. 132/2020/ND-CP imposes a mandatory disallowance of interest on hybrid instruments treated as equity under foreign law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT - GTGT, Giá trị gia tăng) governed by Law No. 13/2008/QH12 as amended by Law No. 31/2013/QH13 and Law No. 106/2016/QH13, implemented by Decree No. 209/2013/ND-CP and Circular No. 219/2013/TT-BTC; revised guidance in Circular No. 102/2024/TT-BTC; temporary reduced rate regime of 8% for specified goods and services under Resolution No. 174/2024/QH15 (in effect until 30 June 2025); administrative penalties under Decree No. 125/2020/ND-CP and customs-related VAT penalties under Decree No. 128/2020/ND-CP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 0 for corporate entities — every LLC must register for VAT at incorporation regardless of initial capital, turnover or duration; there is no de-minimis turnover exemption for companies. For household businesses (hộ kinh doanh) an annual turnover threshold of VND 100,000,000 applies for VAT and CIT exemption under the Law on Tax Administration; such household entities may voluntarily register for VAT. Export processing enterprises (EPE) and cross-border service providers must still obtain an MST and register for the 0% export trader status from the first invoice, and may file quarterly VAT returns on a cash-basis where their turnover is modest.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for all VAT-registered taxpayers under Decree No. 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular No. 78/2021/TT-BTC. E-invoices must be issued in standardized XML (GS1VN data model) and transmitted to the General Department of Taxation via the e-Tax portal or through GDT-certified software using the TCBS API. Most taxpayers operate under the 'invoice authorization code' (Mã của cơ quan thuế) mechanism: the software sends each invoice record to GDT, GDT validates and returns a unique fiscal code, and the invoice is legally valid only after that code is affixed and the data is archived on the GDT server. Paper invoices and pre-printed forms are invalid since 1 July 2022. Retail, catering, petrol and B2C digital platforms must use 'e-cashier invoices' (hóa đơn điện tử khởi tạo từ máy tính tiền) with real-time, line-item clearance through GDT APIs. There is no physical stamping requirement; digital signatures, XML envelopes and reversible QR codes serve as the authenticity seal. For B2B export invoices (including localization services), the taxpayer may use self-generated e-invoices without a CQT code only after completing registration of the invoice form and after validating export documentation; such invoices must be reported to GDT in batch within 24 hours of issuance or at the statutory reporting interval for non-coded invoices, whichever is earlier.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (a) goods physically exported from Viet Nam with a completed customs export declaration; (b) services exported to, and consumed outside Viet Nam by, foreign organizations or individuals that do not have a permanent establishment in Viet Nam (including multilingual translation, subtitling, media localization, voice-over and digital dubbing deliverables); (c) goods and services sold to export processing enterprises or into non-tariff zones; (d) international transportation and related services; (e) processing of goods for export. For a localization agency, the key criteria are: the foreign client is a non-resident entity without a Vietnamese PE; the deliverable is exploited entirely abroad (e.g., subtitled media files delivered to a foreign server or broadcaster); the contract is in writing; payment is remitted via a Vietnamese licensed bank in freely convertible foreign currency or in Vietnamese Dong from a foreign buyer's account only in exceptional State Bank-approved cases; and the service is not a 'domestic consumption' service such as Vietnamese-language proofreading for a local broadcaster, local media adaptation for domestic distribution, or rental of Vietnamese studio facilities. The VAT return (Form 01/GTGT) must show the zero-rated sale, and any excess input VAT is refundable by the GDT quarterly within 40 days for the first refund application and 60 days for subsequent ones, provided the LLC maintains an unbroken chain of VCNC (export) evidence. Revenue from services rendered wholly within Viet Nam even to foreign entities remains subject to the standard 10% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (tờ khai hải quan điện tử) generated through VNACCS/VCIS for physical media, master recordings, or localized packaging; must bear the customs officer's clearance/confirmation and the shipment reference; for digitally delivered localization services, the demonstrating substitute is a Foreign Service Delivery Certificate: an external electronic 'pigeonhole' record showing the server upload/download timestamps, CDN log extraction or a sworn deliverable receipt issued by the foreign client's system;

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (vận đơn đường biển / đường hàng không) covering physical export; for pure digital services, an equivalent 'digital delivery acceptance protocol' signed by the foreign buyer, or a server-side file delivery manifest and email chain;

Commercial invoice in foreign currency with Incoterms and full payment terms; a 0% export e-invoice (Hóa đơn điện tử xuất khẩu) expressly stating 'services/ goods exported and consumed outside Viet Nam';

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC - chứng từ thanh toán qua ngân hàng) or a bank statement evidencing that the foreign buyer's payment in freely convertible currency has been credited to the LLC's Foreign Currency Account or Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA); the IRC must indicate the goods/service invoice number;

Export service contract containing the scope of work, overseas delivery destination and non-PE warranty; a certificate of acceptance signed by the foreign buyer (Biên bản nghiệm thu/ Uỷ quyền nghiệm thu); for EPE sales: non-tariff zone certificate of the buyer and customs declaration E-form;
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The General Department of Taxation and Vietnam Customs conduct desk audits, cross-checked with SWIFT/MT103 records, customs database, and the taxpayer's digital delivery records; for localization companies, the GDT can also verify the foreign client's contract and acceptance history through e-Tax API and request a copy of the foreign maker's payment log. If zero-rating is found to be erroneously claimed, the taxpayer must repay the entire VAT refund plus late-payment interest at 0.02% per day (Law on Tax Administration, Article 59); administrative fines range from 20% to 100% of the under-declared VAT amount, up to VND 100 million for invoicing violations (Decree No. 125/2020/ND-CP). Where documents are forged or a sham foreign transaction is established (e.g., a Vietnamese-affiliated buyer without genuine foreign consumption), the matter becomes tax evasion under the Penal Code 2015, Article 200: criminal liability applies when the evaded amount is at least VND 100 million; individuals face fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment from 1.5 to 7 years; corporate entities face fines up to VND 5 billion, suspension of license and dissolution risk. For smuggling or false customs declarations, Decree No. 128/2020/ND-CP and Penal Code Article 188 impose fines up to 3 times the proceeds and imprisonment up to life. Retrospective clawbacks are permitted for 5 years for standard assessments and 10 years for fraudulent filings; the taxpayer bears the burden of proof. Additional commercial consequences: cancellation of the zero-rating status, revocation of e-invoice issuing rights for 6 to 24 months, blacklisting in the e-Tax portal, and a mandatory 100% VAT prepayment for 12 months after the violation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV; Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam), the central bank and foreign exchange administration authority responsible for exchange-rate policy, capital-account controls, licensing of authorized credit institutions for FX activities, and supervision of cross-border payments and treasury compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam operates a managed-float regime in which the Vietnamese đồng (VND) is not freely convertible outside the licensed interbank market and cross-border capital transactions are heavily controlled. Current-account transactions, including service exports and profit remittances related to genuine operating flows, are generally convertible: an authorized bank may sell foreign currency for import/export, service, and investment-related current payments upon submission of a valid underlying contract, invoice, and tax certificate, with no SBV pre-approval. Capital-account transactions, by contrast, are not freely convertible: foreign equity contributions, shareholder loans, loan repayments, and capital repatriation must be routed through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at an authorized bank, and certain transactions require prior registration with the SBV or the licensed bank. Profit remittance is permissible once annual audited financial statements, a completed corporate income tax finalization, and a tax-obligation clearance/confirmation are obtained; in practice, banks will block an outward remittance that lacks the audited statement, tax finalization, and board resolution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For an ISIC 7490 localization service exporter, all foreign-currency receipts from non-resident clients are service export proceeds and must be credited to a foreign-currency account at an SBV-licensed bank in Viet Nam. The statutory benchmark is that proceeds are repatriated no later than the contractual due date; where the contract is silent, the bank applies a 90-day window from the invoice/service-completion date. There is currently no mandatory percentage-surrender ratio in force for service export earnings; exporters may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency and elect to sell them to the authorized bank when VND liquidity is needed. The SBV retains emergency reserve power to impose a temporary surrender ratio in periods of severe balance-of-payments pressure, in which case the ratio would be published in an SBV decision and applied from its effective date. The treasurer should maintain original signed localization agreements, per-invoice reconciliation, and MT103/MT202 payment evidence to demonstrate timely repatriation and to support the lawfulness of retained foreign-currency balances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA)/Capital Escrow Account; USD-denominated FX account and VND operational account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade (VietinBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA)/Capital Escrow Account; USD-denominated FX account and VND operational account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam (BIDV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA)/Capital Escrow Account; multi-currency and VND operational account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank (Techcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA)/Capital Escrow Account; VND operational account and USD/foreign-currency account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional and ancillary only. Wise B2B and Payoneer are unlicensed foreign EMI/payment-service providers in Viet Nam and cannot be used as a primary treasury clearing rail, a VND current account, or a capital-account channel. They are acceptable as a collection-side convenience for low-risk localization fees from non-resident clients, provided all funds are ultimately settled through a local sponsor bank into the VN company's bank account, each inbound credit is reconciled to a specific invoice and service-export declaration, and the company maintains its complete cash/fiscal position in onshore licensed accounts. The SBV does not recognize these EMIs as authorized credit institutions; using them to circumvent DICA rules or to receive equity capital would be unlawful.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a 100% foreign-invested LLC, physical presence and in-person KYC are the practical rule. Viet Nam's AML and bank KYC standards require the legal representative or a director holding an in-country power of attorney to attend an interview and biometric verification at the opening bank; remote-only onboarding is not available for foreign-owned entities. Most tier-1 banks also perform a site visit or accept a certified lease agreement plus utility bills, staff photographs, and business-equipment inventory to verify operational substance. The optimal approach is for one executive to travel to Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City for 5–10 business days to sign account mandates, answer AML questions, and provide wet-ink/notarized documentation for the legal representative and UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO/control-chain opacity: ultimate beneficial owners are foreign individuals or parents in a jurisdiction with no treaty or an offshore structure, and the intermediary owner does not have audited accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration; complete corporate ownership tree to natural persons; passport copies; certificate of incorporation and register of members for each intermediate holding entity; audited financial statements of the immediate parent for the last 2 years; bank/solicitor references for the parent; and a board resolution of the foreign parent appointing the VN legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-account mismatch: the inward remittance amount, sender, or purpose code does not match the IRC, charter, or capital-contribution schedule, or funds arrive before the DICA is opened.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investment Registration Certificate (IRC); Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); fully executed charter and capital-contribution schedule; capital call/board resolution; DICA opening certificate; source-of-funds statement from the remitting bank; and a signed confirmation that no prior contribution has been made.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service revenue red flag: large and frequent SWIFT receipts from non-resident clients without a clear commercial underlying, physically-substantiated service delivery, or tax filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed localization agreements, purchase orders, per-invoice reconciliation ledger; detailed translation/dubbing work orders and completion certificates; VAT/CIT filing receipts and audited financial statements; sample quality-delivery materials; and a completed AML questionnaire covering client industry and beneficial owner status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment/pooling via Wise, Payoneer, or client-side aggregators: bank sees a fintech intermediary as remitter/receiver and flags potential layering or unverifiable end-client funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written agreements with the ultimate payers; Wise/Payoneer account statements showing underlying transaction references; payment-service-provider attestation or SOW; reconciliation of each inbound transfer to a specific invoice; and a board-approved treasury policy committing the company to invoice-level settlement and immediate transfer of all EMI collections into the onshore bank account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The investor initiates a SWIFT MT103 from its offshore bank to the VN LLC's DICA at the onshore licensed bank. Beneficiary account must be the DICA; Payment Details/Remittance Information must identify the IRC number, the entity name, and the purpose 'equity capital contribution'. The receiving bank reconciles the message against the DICA, IRC, ERC, charter, and the registered capital-contribution schedule before crediting. Once credited, the foreign-currency balance may be sold to VND at that bank's published exchange rate for operating liquidity; conversion is treated as a separate FX transaction and cannot be effected directly inside the DICA. Any subsequent movement from the DICA to the company's ordinary VND/FX operating account requires a board resolution or capital-utilization note describing the operating purpose. Equity remittances that are denominated in a non-USD currency should be converted into USD at an offshore bank before transmission, or accepted only if the VN bank explicitly agrees to multi-currency DICA crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary rail for service-provider payments is SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the LLC's licensed-account treasury. For counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions or for large engagements, the bank will require the underlying localization/subcontract agreement, an invoice, proof of service acceptance, and the foreign contractor withholding tax certificate (VAT/CIT certificates) before executing the transfer. For physical deliverables such as dubbing or subtitling equipment integrated into localization work, an irrevocable sight letter of credit issued under UCP600 through Vietcombank/VietinBank/BIDV is the prudent commercial-clearing rail, with the shipping documents routed through the advising bank. VND-denominated disbursements to domestic suppliers can be cleared via NAPAS 24/7 or standard local ACH. Wise B2B/Payoneer may be used only for small operational payments to pre-approved overseas contractors, and must never replace a documented, bank-verified trade settlement where a VAT/customs or foreign-contractor-tax trigger exists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore VND/USD deliverable outright forward contracts (tenor up to 365 days) with documented underlying service-export or payable exposure, executed through an SBV-licensed credit institution
Onshore VND/USD FX swaps combining spot and forward legs, suitable for temporary VND/USD liquidity stacking around capital inflows and quarterly fee collections
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (principal and interest exchange between USD and VND) for SBV-registered shareholder loans or project financing

European-style VND/USD currency options or cost-reducing option structures (collars, participating forwards) offered by licensed banks, subject to the bank's product approval and the company's demonstrated underlying treasury risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) / National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year reporter this falls on 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission triggers administrative fines of approx. USD 400-800 (VND 10,000,000-20,000,000) under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; failure to file for two consecutive fiscal years allows DPI to declare the enterprise non-operational and ultimately revoke the Enterprise Registration Certificate (strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Licence Tax (Lệ phí môn bài)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District-level Tax Office (Chi cục Thuế) via the eTax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable no later than 30 January each year; newly established enterprises are exempt for the first fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs interest at 0.03% per day (approx. 10.95% per annum) and late-filing administrative fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; repeated delinquency enables the competent Tax Office to impose compulsory bank-account levy and asset distraint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Finalisation Return (Quyết toán thuế TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation / operational District Tax Office via eTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Dually filed within 90 days of fiscal year-end (in practice 31 March for a calendar-year accounting period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalised progressively from VND 2,000,000 to VND 25,000,000 (approx. USD 80-1,000) per Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; underpaid CIT additionally carries 0.03% daily late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposition of Audited Financial Statements with the business registration and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DPI and the General Department of Taxation (co-submission requirement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from the fiscal year-end, simultaneously with the Annual Enterprise Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit audited financial statements incurs administrative fines up to VND 20,000,000 (approx. USD 800) and blocks the foreign investor's profit remittance declaration for the reporting year; the DPI may treat persistent non-compliance as a basis for strike-off review.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory annual independent audit for all foreign-invested enterprises, including a 100% foreign-owned LLC, irrespective of revenue or asset size (Article 3 Decree 17/2012/ND-CP). Domestic non-FIE LLCs are captured only above thresholds of VND 50 billion total assets or VND 30 billion annual revenue; this entity is FIE and therefore always in-scope.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) in accordance with the Law on Accounting 2015 and Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; voluntary full IFRS application under Decree 132/2021 is not adopted for this SME localization entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Equity transfers and changes in the LLC member/contributor list must be recorded in the Register of Members and notified to the DPI within 15 days of the triggering transaction (Law on Enterprises 2020, Article 30). The Annual Enterprise Report confirms the final member schedule, capital contribution ratios and intra-year ownership movements as at fiscal year-end. No separate stand-alone UBO annual return is prescribed for a private unlisted FIE LLC, but banks and payment-service providers must maintain beneficial-owner identification data under the AML Law 2022.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Danh sách thành viên)
Register of Directors and Legal Representative changes
Minute Book of member/owner meetings and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-600 per annum for a standard registered-office or licensed agent address in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City; premium serviced-office identity packages range USD 800-1,500.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800-2,500 per statutory audit engagement for a small-capitalisation foreign-invested LLC using local licensed audit firms; Big Four engagement fees typically range USD 3,000-6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard headline CIT rate for a foreign-invested limited liability company in Viet Nam is 20%. No blanket sectoral CIT incentive applies for ISIC 7490 (translation/localization). However, preferential rates and tax holidays may apply if the enterprise qualifies for high-technology enterprise status (10% for 15 years), or if the activity is located in encouraged investment zones (e.g., industrial parks, economic zones, high-tech parks) or qualifies as a socialized sector under Decree 154/2020. Software production activities may enjoy a 10% preferential CIT rate for up to 15 years. For a typical localization agency engaged only in translation, media dubbing and related services, the 20% statutory rate is the operative assumption unless investment incentives are expressly granted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly provisional CIT return - Form 01/TNDN, filed electronically via the National Tax Electronic Portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn) or via a certified tax service provider.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 30th day of the first month following the end of the quarter. Example: Q1 (January–March) is due by 30 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax code, address, legal representative, and contact information of the VN LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Vietnamese tax identification number (MST) and the full registered Vietnamese name of the LLC; the foreign parent is identified only in the accompanying schedules.
Use the VN LLC's fiscal year Quarter 1–4; if the entity uses a different fiscal year than calendar, state the correct quarter mapping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales, service revenue, dubbing and localization fees, translation fees, and incidental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all amounts receivable from foreign group companies via Wise or Payoneer in Vietnamese Dong (VND); foreign currency is converted at the actual transaction rate or the official cross-rate announced by the State Bank of Viet Nam.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: salaries, subcontracting, rent, utilities, software licenses, amortization, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses supported by valid invoices and vouchers per Circular 96/2015 are deductible; intercompany charges must be supported by arm's length transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as revenue minus deductible expenses and non-taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include capital gains or dividends already tax-exempt; quarterly provisional income is based on actual quarter results unless the entity elects the simplified 80% of prior-year method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT losses brought forward from prior years, up to a maximum of 5 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The carryforward is applied only when the current quarter is profitable; the loss amount must be traceable to annual finalization returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable headline rate, ordinarily 20%, or preferential rate if approved.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the rate corresponding to the tax incentive decision, if any; otherwise enter 20%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by CIT rate, then reduced by any investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly advance payment must be at least 80% of the final CIT liability; a supplementary payment is required on finalization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Differences between previously declared amounts and current quarter estimates, including any additional payments or decreases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no prior quarter amounts exist, enter zero; the VN LLC should retain bank transfer evidence for quarterly payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the quarterly return attracts an administrative fine from VND 1,000,000 to VND 25,000,000 depending on the number of days late. Late payment of quarterly CIT advance is subject to automatic late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the outstanding amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual CIT finalization return - Form 02/TNDN, submitted electronically via the National Tax Electronic Portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn) together with audited financial statements and the TP disclosure form (Form 01/TNDN? - Form 01 was quarterly; annual appendices include Form 02-1/TNDN and related schedules).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 90 days from the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 30 March of the following year (or 31 August for fiscal-year taxpayers if their approved fiscal year ends on any date other than 31 December, with the 90-day rule applicable).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax code, address, legal representative, field of operation (ISIC 7490).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match business registration certificate. If the foreign parent is the ultimate beneficiary, this line does not require identification of the parent unless requested in the appendix.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 02 – Revenue from goods and services (Mã chỉ tiêu 02)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total annual revenue, including localization income, translation and dubbing fees, and other sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all revenue actually accrued, regardless of where payment is made. Cross-border electronical payment rails merely provide settlement; revenue is Vat-able and CIT-able in Viet Nam.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income that is exempt from CIT under the Law on Corporate Income Tax, e.g., income from government-fund research, certain capital contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The burden of substantiating an exemption is on the taxpayer; for a localization agency, non-taxable income is typically nil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual costs incurred in generating taxable revenue, limited to those with adequate invoices and lawful supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany localization-related expenses (e.g., overseas studio fees, software licensing) are deductible only to the extent that they are arm's length, economically substantiated, and supported by a TP file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue (line 02) minus deductible expenses (line 04) minus non-taxable income (line 03).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is negative, the loss is carried forward to subsequent years; no negative annual tax liability exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 06 – Losses from prior years (Mã chỉ tiêu 06)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward from previous years, offset up to 5 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss offset should be computed on a calendar-year basis and the evidence of the prior-year return must be retained.
If tax incentives apply, attach the investment license or tax authority approval confirming the preferential rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 08 – CIT payable for the year (Mã chỉ tiêu 08)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income, reduced by any tax credits, tax holidays, or foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute on the basis of final annual figures, not quarterly estimates. Foreign tax credits are allowed only if a DTA applies and the foreign tax was actually paid abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 09 – Advance CIT paid during the year (Mã chỉ tiêu 09)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match to bank receipts from the eTax system or the state treasury; any overpayment will be credited or refundable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 – Additional tax payable / refund (Mã chỉ tiêu 10)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between the annual CIT payable and the sum of advance quarterly payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the quarterly advance was less than 80% of final liability, the company will be charged late-payment interest on the shortfall. Any refund should be requested on Form 02/DNT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late finalization return: administrative fine up to VND 25,000,000 if the return is filed more than 90 days late; failure to pay tax on time triggers late-payment interest at 0.03% per day. Incorrect or false declaration with underpaid tax results in a penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax amount if not detected as tax evasion; intentional evasion is prosecuted under the Penal Code. The legal representative cannot be granted an exit visa while tax arrears remain outstanding.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Viet Nam does not impose dividend withholding tax on distributions from a Vietnamese limited liability company to a foreign corporate shareholder). Repatriation of after-tax profits is governed by Law on Investment and foreign exchange control. The VN LLC must complete the annual profit remittance dossier to the Investment Registration Agency and State Bank licensed bank.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because domestic law imposes no dividend WHT, no dividend treaty claim is necessary. For royalties and interest subject to Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT), a non-resident seeking treaty relief must submit a Treaty Relief Application (Form 01/HT) together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, and, where requested, an explanation of substance and activities performed. The VN LLC (payor) must retain these documents and apply the treaty-reduced rate at the time of payment. If the treaty rate has not been applied because documentation was incomplete, the non-resident may file for a refund within the statute of limitations (usually 10 years under the Law on Tax Administration) through the Vietnamese payor or through a direct Vietnamese tax office filing.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic FCT rates: royalties (IP licenses, software copyrights, media dubbing rights) are subject to CIT at 10% of the gross royalty amount, plus VAT at 5% or 0% depending on the nature of the license (for pure copyright licence royalty, VAT is 0%; for service-like software, the applicable VAT/CIT may be 5% CIT and 5% VAT). Interest on shareholder loans and intercompany debt is subject to FCT CIT at 5%; interest is VAT-exempt. Under Viet Nam's DTAs, treaty rates for royalties are commonly 10% (many older treaties) and for copyright royalties 5% (if provided); interest rates are typically 10%, with some treaties reducing interest to 5% for financial institutions and to 0% for government debt. Actual treaty rates depend on the specific DTA between Viet Nam and the country of residence of the recipient (e.g., China, Japan, South Korea and the US commonly entitle a 10% or 5% rate). Claiming treaty relief requires beneficial ownership and no Limitation-on-Benefits violation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: VND 50 billion total annual revenue or VND 30 billion total related-party transaction value (whichever applies) triggers mandatory preparation of a Local File. In addition, if the ultimate parent group (whether in Viet Nam or abroad) has consolidated revenue exceeding VND 18,000 billion or total consolidated assets exceeding VND 20,000 billion, the VN LLC must prepare a Master File. Country-by-Country (CbC) report is mandatory when the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue exceeds VND 18,000 billion. These thresholds are set out in Decree 132/2020/ND-CP and Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Viet Nam's transfer pricing and anti-avoidance framework under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP requires that related-party transactions have genuine economic substance and be structured with a sound business purpose. Article 17 specifically allows tax authorities to re-characterize transactions that lack economic substance, including transactions whose primary objective is to obtain tax benefits without actual commercial reality. For a localization agency owning minimal staff, no operating premises, or contracts that merely channel payments to a foreign affiliate, the substance doctrine may invalidate deductions, add deemed income, and impose penalties. The General Department of Taxation also applies an Economic Substance guidance consistent with OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) Action 3 principles. The VN LLC must be able to demonstrate real functions, assets, risks, and decision-making in Viet Nam.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / False corporate income tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of localization revenue (including digital translation and dubbing fees remitted through Wise/Payoneer), overstatement of deductible expenses, use of fake invoices, understated intercompany income, or omission of offshore bank accounts related to VN LLC activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Vietnamese Penal Code 2015 (Article 200 as amended 2017), legal entities that commit tax evasion with improper revenue exceeding VND 100 million are subject to fines ranging from VND 300 million to VND 4.5 billion; natural persons (directors, controllers) face fines up to VND 4.5 billion and/or prison terms of 1 to 20 years, depending on the amount illegally evaded. Administrative sanctions in lesser cases include a penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax, plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day and potential suspension of business operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives, chief accountants, and controlling shareholders can personally be held criminally liable. Courts can pierce the corporate veil if the company is an alter ego of the director; assets of the director may be seized for civil restitution. Exit bans (travel bans) are automatically applicable for unpaid tax debts until repayment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / Lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a paper LLC with no employees, no dedicated office, no actual translation/dubbing activities, no accounting records; using the VN entity merely to book profit and shift income to a tax-free jurisdiction; engaging in back-to-back contracts without adding value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authorities may re-characterize the entire business as a conduit arrangement, disallow all deductible expenses, assess CIT at 20% with a 20% penalty on underpaid tax, impose late-payment interest, and, for 3 consecutive years, escalate to criminal tax evasion. The tax authority may also refuse to issue tax finalization certificates or PTI (Payment of Tax – Income) documents necessary for profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for the whole tax deficiency where they knowingly orchestrated the shell arrangement. Civil restitution, dissolution, and travel bans apply; criminal imprisonment is possible if the arrangement defrauds the State of more than VND 1 billion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany fees for localization or media dubbing services at non-arm's length levels (e.g., exorbitant royalties payable to an offshore parent; paying for services never performed; allocating significant Vietnamese profit to a foreign affiliate through artificially high cost-plus margins).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vietnamese tax authorities can apply TP adjustments, recalculate taxable income, and impose penalties of 20% of the underpaid tax plus late-payment interest of 0.03% per day. Failure to submit TP documentation or CbC report may result in administrative fines of VND 20 million to VND 50 million; an adjusted TP audit may also be criminalized if deemed intentional evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and chief financial officers who sign documentation or approve transactions may be subject to administrative fines and criminal liability for fraud. Courts may annul the separate legal personality of the subsidiary and attach personal assets of the director if the intercompany pricing was structured to circumvent tax obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using offshore payment rails (Wise, Payoneer) to receive localization fees without recording the income in VN accounts, failing to declare foreign-currency receipts, splitting payments to avoid the tax threshold, or knowingly receiving proceeds from clients involved in money laundering, without filing STR under the AML Law (Law 04/2012/QH13 as amended).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Penal Code 2015 Article 324, money laundering by a legal entity is punishable by fines up to VND 20 billion; natural persons who are directors or beneficial owners face imprisonment of 2 to 15 years. Violations of foreign exchange control provisions can lead to administrative fines up to VND 200 million, forced repatriation, and suspension of payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers can be personally arrested and imprisoned; assets can be frozen; travel bans apply; the corporate veil is pierced if the company is operated as a vehicle for laundering criminal proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The VN LLC makes payments to non-resident shareholders or overseas suppliers for royalties (e.g., software license, dubbing rights) or interest on shareholder/intercompany loans without determining FCT and without withholding the required 5%–10% CIT (and 5% VAT if applicable).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The VN LLC as withholding agent is liable for the unwithheld FCT amount, plus a penalty of 20% of the underwithheld tax and late-payment interest at 0.03% per day. The deductible expense paid abroad is disallowed for CIT purposes until the FCT is settled. Repeated violations can trigger criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or knowingly allow the non-withholding may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate debt; criminal proceedings may be instituted for intentional failure. Travel bans and property attachment are available enforcement measures.
